cards.title: Legions
cards.summary: Rome's professional heavy infantry: ~5,000 citizen soldiers per legion.

cards.title: Roads
cards.summary: 80,000 km of paved roads that moved armies, mail and trade.

cards.title: Emperors
cards.summary: From Augustus in 27 BC to Romulus Augustulus in AD 476.

cards.title: Why did it fall?
cards.summary: Historians still argue: money, plague, migration, civil wars.

cards.title: Why Rome won so much
cards.summary: Not better weapons — better organisation, and refusing to quit.

cards.title: Equipment
cards.summary: Gladius, pilum, scutum, and segmented armour.

cards.title: A soldier's life
cards.summary: 25 years of service, marching 30 km a day.

cards.title: Discipline
cards.summary: Drill every day; harsh punishments; units that held formation.

cards.title: Logistics
cards.summary: Food, roads and camps meant armies could stay in the field.

cards.title: Allies
cards.summary: Conquered peoples supplied troops — and later became citizens.

cards.title: Marching camps
cards.summary: A fortified camp built every night, same layout everywhere.

cards.title: Grain supply
cards.summary: Each soldier ate about 1 kg of grain a day.
